paragraphs.source_en: At this point Meitei evidently decided that the man was beyond salvation, and, quite unlike his usual self, fell silent. From Meitei's side, he considered that my master's worth declined in proportion as he grew more obstinate. From the master's side, however, the more stubbornly he held to his view, the more he thought he had risen a step above Meitei. There are plenty of such absurd cross-purposes in the world. While a man imagines that he will win if only he persists in obstinacy, his value as a person drops headlong. The strange thing is that such an obstinate fellow goes to his grave believing he has saved face, never dreaming that from that time on people have despised him and refused to have anything more to do with him. This pleasure that seeks only a moment's satisfaction is said to have a name: piggish happiness.
